title: Household Finance Brokerage Platform Competitive Landscape

scope.description: Brokers, comparison sites and public comparison tools that compete for the same Belgian households and jobs as Peasy, the Zaventem-based 'phygital' household-finance brokerage modeled in this domain (hypotheek.winkel mortgage offices comparing 25 banks, Verzekeringen.be / Assurances.be insurance comparison across 11 insurers, Aanbieders.be / Mesfournisseurs.be energy and telecom switching): first-time buyers and refinancers who need a mortgage compared and closed, and families who want to cut fixed costs on insurance, energy and telecom without doing the paperwork. Peasy itself is not listed as a player; its own figures (>150 experts, 70 offices, >50,000 contracts per year, >50 partners, about 200 employees and roughly EUR 30 million revenue) are the yardstick against which each entry is positioned.
inclusionLogic: mortgage broker networks with physical offices and multi-bank comparison, the head-to-head alternative to a hypotheek.winkel appointment for a Belgian home buyer
credit intermediaries and credit-comparison sites that a refinancer, renovator or consumer-credit borrower would consult instead of uploading a proposal to Peasy
digital insurance brokers that bind and monitor a household's policies online, competing with Verzekeringen.be and Peasy's contract-monitoring promise
energy and telecom comparators with phone advisors or self-service switching, competing directly with Aanbieders.be for the switch and the referral fee

public, non-commercial comparison tools run by the FSMA and the Flemish energy regulator, which do not earn commissions but set the reference point for independence and can absorb the self-service comparison a household would otherwise start on peasy.be
notes: Business stats are only included when they appear on the player's own official website (home, about, press pages); each stat keeps the reported scope and period as published. Players for which no official figure could be verified (Credishop, TopCompare.be) carry no business stats rather than estimates.

Players report at different scopes: Immotheker Finotheker publishes cumulative loans concluded and product counts, Yago publishes a customer count and a post-claim recommendation rate, Meilleurtaux reports group-level history and its Belgian entry; none of these are directly comparable with Peasy's >50,000 contracts per year, which spans mortgage, insurance, energy and telecom.

Meilleurtaux Belgium is a special case: it competed with Peasy in Wallonia after entering Belgium in 2023 through MiD Finance, and in December 2025 agreed to acquire 100 percent of Peasy, creating a combined network of 81 offices; it is kept as a player because its consumer-credit and credit-grouping proposition remains the reference for the adjacent scope of this domain.

Wikifin (FSMA) and the VREG V-test / V-check are public programmes without a commercial model; they are listed because they are explicitly excluded from Peasy's scope in DOMAIN.md and shape what households expect a free, independent comparison to look like.
Logos under business/logos/ are placeholders to be replaced with official brand assets.

players.name: Immotheker Finotheker
players.description: Immotheker Finotheker is an independent, Belgium-wide mortgage and financial broker network and the most direct competitor of hypotheek.winkel. It positions itself as '100% independent', opened its first office on 1 April 1995 in Schoten, runs a mortgage monitor since 2004, introduced an attestation of purchase security in 2024 and reports 100 offices, 150 employees, more than 10,000 products compared, more than 55,000 loans concluded and 30 years of experience. It compares more than 2,000 mortgage loans at 16 banks daily. Founders are John Romain, Alex Geens and Jan Romain. Versus Peasy: a larger Belgium-wide office footprint and a longer track record in mortgage brokerage, but a narrower bank panel (16 versus 25 banks compared daily) and no insurance, energy and telecom comparison brands, so it competes for the mortgage appointment rather than for the whole household relationship.

players.name: Meilleurtaux Belgium
players.description: Meilleurtaux Belgium is the Belgian arm of the French credit and insurance broker Meilleurtaux (founded 1999, majority-owned by Silver Lake since 2020). It entered Belgium in 2023 through the acquisition of MiD Finance and is active mainly in Wallonia, with offices in Ghent and Antwerp, offering personal loans, credit grouping, mortgage, car and renovation loans and insurance. On 23 December 2025 Meilleurtaux agreed to acquire 100 percent of Peasy, creating a national platform with 81 offices led in Belgium and Luxembourg by Peasy CEO David Geerts. Versus Peasy: until the agreement it was a competitor in Wallonia, the Walloon mirror image of hypotheek.winkel with a stronger consumer-credit and credit-grouping offer; after the deal it is the group Peasy integrates with, bringing shared bank and insurer relationships and the consumer-credit products Peasy adds in its year-one horizon.

players.name: Credishop
players.description: Credishop is an independent Belgian credit intermediary in mortgage credit and instalment loans that emphasises personal service and focuses on renovation and energy loans. Versus Peasy: a small, relationship-driven intermediary that competes for the refinancer and renovator who wants one trusted advisor, without Peasy's office network, daily 25-bank comparison, simulators or cross-brand insurance, energy and telecom offer. No business statistics are published on its official site, so none are listed.

players.name: Yago (formerly Seraphin)
players.description: Yago, formerly Seraphin, is a Brussels-based digital insurance broker recognised by the FSMA. It manages all of a household's insurance contracts in a single digital interface, reports more than 30,000 customers, states that in 2025 97 percent of customers recommend it after a claim and promises a customer-service response within 2 hours. Versus Peasy: the purest digital alternative to Verzekeringen.be and to Peasy's contract-monitoring promise for insurance, with a stronger claims-service story; it has no mortgage offices, no energy and telecom switching and no physical advisory network, so it competes for the insurance relationship rather than for the mortgage-led household.

players.name: CallMePower
players.description: CallMePower is a free comparison and advice service for energy, broadband, mobile, TV, insurance and moving in Belgium. Phone advisors compare offers and execute the switch for the household. It is part of the Selectra group, founded in 2007 and active in 18 countries. Versus Peasy: the closest mirror of Aanbieders.be and of the Hasselt and Oujda customer-care model (phone advisors who compare and switch, free for the household), backed by an international group; it lacks the mortgage offices, the feasibility certificate and the household contract vault that let Peasy start from the mortgage and expand into fixed costs.

players.name: DareToCompare.be / DurfBesparen.be
players.description: DareToCompare.be (DurfBesparen.be) is an independent energy and telecom comparator for families and the self-employed, founded (relaunched) in 2021 by Evert Engelen, who has more than 20 years of market experience and launched the first Belgian online energy and telecom comparator in 2007. Versus Peasy: a lean, founder-led self-service comparator that competes with Aanbieders.be for the online energy and telecom switch; it has no mortgage offer, no office network of experts and no contract-monitoring relationship, so its edge is speed and independence for the household that wants to switch alone.

businessStats.value: founded (relaunched) in 2021 by Evert Engelen; first Belgian online energy and telecom comparator launched in 2007; 20+ years of market experience

players.name: TopCompare.be
players.description: TopCompare.be is a Brussels-based financial comparison site covering personal loans, mortgages, credit cards, bank accounts and insurance policies. Versus Peasy: it captures the first online research step of a refinancer or consumer-credit borrower and hands the lead to lenders, without simulators tied to an office appointment, expert-assembled credit files or switch execution; it competes for the upload-your-proposal and consumer-credit traffic rather than for the concluded contract. No verified business statistics are available on its official site, so none are listed.

players.name: Wikifin (FSMA)
players.description: Wikifin is the financial-education programme of the Belgian financial regulator FSMA, launched on 31 January 2013. It is non-commercial and offers independent information, a savings-account comparison tool and the IMMOsimulator for home-purchase costs, plus Wikifin School and the Wikifin Lab. Versus Peasy: it does not broker or earn commissions and is explicitly outside Peasy's scope, but its neutral simulators and comparison tools are where many first-time buyers start before booking an appointment, and they set the public benchmark for what an independent comparison should disclose.

players.name: VREG V-test and V-check
players.description: The V-test and V-check are the public, non-commercial energy-contract comparison tools of the Flemish energy regulator VREG. The V-test compares electricity and gas contracts; the V-check reads the invoice code that suppliers must print on invoices since 1 July 2025 to pre-fill the comparison, and VRT NWS reported tens of thousands of uses in its first two months. Versus Peasy: it is the reference households and journalists use to judge whether a commercial comparator is honest, it takes no commission and executes no switch, so Aanbieders.be competes by adding the advisor, the switch execution and the monitoring that the V-test deliberately leaves to the consumer.
